CC: Confusion and fever.

HPI (per daughter): 78-year-old man with dementia who over 2 days became more confused, agitated, and febrile to 101.8 F. Decreased oral intake, new urinary incontinence. No cough, no abdominal pain, no vomiting. Daughter notes foul-smelling urine. No recent falls, no head trauma.

PMH: Dementia, BPH, hypertension.

Home meds: Donepezil 10 mg nightly; Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; Lisinopril 10 mg daily.

Allergies: Sulfa (hives).

SH: Lives with daughter. Baseline: conversant, ambulates with walker.

ROS: Fever, confusion, dysuria per daughter. Unable to obtain further history from patient.

Exam:
VS: T 101.2 F, HR 108, BP 96/62, RR 20, SpO2 94% RA.
General: Elderly man, inattentive, picking at sheets.
HEENT: Dry mucous membranes.
CV: Tachycardic, regular.
Abd: Soft, suprapubic tenderness.
Neuro: Disoriented, inattentive; no focal deficits.

Objective:
Labs: WBC 15.8 (H), Lactate 2.8 (H), Creatinine 1.9 (H), BUN 38, UA: large leuk esterase, positive nitrites.
Blood cultures: Pending.
Urine culture: Pending.

Assessment: 78-year-old man with altered mental status and fever, concerning for urosepsis.

Plan:
1. Severe sepsis, likely urinary source
- Broad-spectrum antibiotics (cefepime per allergy history)
- 30 mL/kg crystalloid bolus, reassess perfusion
- Blood cultures drawn before antibiotics

2. Acute kidney injury
- Monitor UOP, daily BMP
- Avoid nephrotoxins

3. Delirium superimposed on dementia
- Reorientation, avoid restraints and sedatives
- Review medications for anticholinergics
